data.name: Ashnoor
data.gender_notes: Ashnoor is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Ashnoor is a Sanskrit name derived from the Asha tree and the word 'noor', which means light. It symbolizes the radiance of the moonlight on the night sky. In Hindu mythology, it is believed that the Asha tree is a wish-fulfilling tree, and the name Ashnoor is given to girls born under the auspicious moonlight. The name Ashnoor carries the meaning “Moonlight, Night Sky” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Ashnoor usually hope their child will grow to embody moonlight, night sky and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ashnoor total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

The Asha tree is considered sacred in Hinduism, and it is believed that if one prays under this tree, their wishes will be granted, adding to the idea of the name's meaning. historical_references.reference: Ashnoor was a legendary queen of the Vidharbha region in ancient India. She is a central character in the epic Sanskrit poem 'Mahabharata'. During a war between the Pandavas and Kauravas, Ashnoor, disguised as a eunuch, entered the Pandava camp to spy on them. However, she was discovered and captured. Bhima, one of the Pandavas, was infatuated with her and decided to marry her. Even after revealing her true identity, Bhima did not abandon her. Instead, he granted her the kingdom of Vidharbha.

Ashnoor is also the name of a temple town in the Indian state of Maharashtra. It is believed that this place was once ruled by a queen named Ashnoor. Ashnoor was a very pious queen who was known for her devotion to Lord Shiva. According to legend, when the temple of Lord Shiva in Ashnoor was being constructed, King Ashnoor dreamt of a heavenly Nandi (the bull vehicle of Lord Shiva) appearing before him. He took it as a divine sign and ordered the construction of a grand temple dedicated to Lord Shiva. Today, Ashnoor is a popular pilgrimage site for Shiv devotees.

She is best known for her roles in popular shows like 'Anupamaa' on Star Plus, 'Aladdin-Naam Tera' on ALTBalaji, and 'Guddan Tumse Na Ho Payega' on Voot. Ashnoor's acting skills, coupled with her youthful charm and versatility, have made her a fan favorite across various platforms.
